title: Cities: Skylines | Franklin, Episode 9: Organized Labor
premise: Donoteat01 argues that collective, explicitly anti-racist labor organization wins material gains and should protect workers rather than merely preserve jobs within capitalism. Roman plebeians, Luddites and the 1835 Philadelphia-inspired general strike frame a modern union taxonomy interrupted by a deliberately fabricated Jimmy Hoffa rescue adventure.
coverage: Municipal-service footage opens a labor-history lecture over city construction, interrupted by historical images, cartoons and a fabricated Hoffa adventure. Cut times are approximate, and brief inserts may be missed. Historical claims are the presenter’s; the Hoffa rescue is a tall tale.

panels.heading: Crony-capitalism caption callback

panels.action: City editor remains visible behind lettering.
panels.visualGag: Exact typographic callback to the earlier crony-capitalism label, mocking the inadequate alternative to a structural critique; prepares the later long Rothschilds-substitution caption.

panels.heading: Corporatism: second euphemism callback

panels.action: Player continues rail-yard editing beneath the word.
panels.visualGag: Second rejected euphemism repeats the early-caption sequence; connects CRONY CAPITALISM to the immediately following overlong, racially diverse bankers/Rothschilds caption.
panels.notes: The corporatism label is a rejected explanation.

panels.heading: Scapegoat callback
panels.description: Long quoted caption about a multi-ethnic racially diverse group of greedy bankers includes triple-parenthesized THE ROTHSCHILDS.
panels.camera: Static image cuts in over gameplay or black.
panels.visualGag: The long caption recalls the rejected conspiracy and echoed Rothschilds gag. Its triple-parentheses lettering mocks antisemitic scapegoating rather than endorsing it.

panels.camera: Static image cuts in over gameplay or black.
panels.visualGag: Clown/carnival substitution punctures repeated union recruitment while the giant ORGANIZE caption persists: connected to original poster and comic-worker variants, and followed by WORLD DOMINATION.
